title: How far is the rabbit from the nearest thousand?
description: Meera's rabbit now has food a thousand apart. The video counts the jumps each way, then shows what happens when the rabbit sits exactly halfway.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the jumps to the thousand on each side; exactly halfway goes to the bigger one by agreement. Watch for a child who thinks any big last part means go up.

source: The rabbit is at 2,346 and its food is at 2,000 and 3,000. W
video_script.why: The child has found the nearest ten and hundred, but not the nearest thousand, nor a number exactly halfway.
video_script.substitution: Count the jumps to the two thousands, choose the fewer, and send an exact halfway to the bigger one.
video_script.anchor: Meera's pet rabbit hopping along a numbered garden path in Pune
video_script.wrong_answer: so the rabbit goes up to three thousand
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu sees three hundred and forty six as big and goes up. The rabbit is nearer to two thousand, because three hundred and forty six is less than half of one thousand.
video_script.payoff_line: three hundred and forty six jumps is fewer than six hundred and fifty four

final_answer.value: 2,000 is the nearest thousand of 2,346, with 346 jumps
final_answer.spoken: two thousand with three hundred and forty six jumps

maths_rules: exactly halfway: 2,500 is 500 from 2,000 and 500 from 3,000; by agreement it goes to the bigger one, 3,000
video_script.design: One idea: count the jumps, and a tie goes to the bigger. The same rabbit and path stay as the anchor; the long number line builds on the stage.

<bookmark mark='def'/>The thousand with the fewest jumps is called the nearest thousand.

<bookmark mark='sub'/>Three thousand take away two thousand three hundred and forty six leaves six hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Three hundred and forty six jumps is fewer than six hundred and fifty four jumps. The rabbit goes to two thousand.

<bookmark mark='tie'/>Both foods are five hundred jumps away, so the jumps cannot decide.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By agreement, a number exactly halfway goes to the bigger neighbour, three thousand.
